title: U.S. House · Utah's 3rd District
area: Southern and eastern Utah under the congressional map first used in 2026, drawn by a Third District Court after the Legislature's 2021 map was struck down; largely overlaps the old 2nd District, including Cedar City, St. George and southeastern Utah.

context.text: Utah's congressional map was redrawn for 2026 by court order in League of Women Voters v. Utah State Legislature. Incumbent Celeste Maloy — who previously represented the old 2nd District — is running for this newly drawn 3rd District. Maloy defeated Phil Lyman 68.1%-31.9% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary.

candidates.name: Celeste Maloy
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Phil Lyman 68.1%-31.9% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Celeste Maloy is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election, running in the newly drawn 3rd District after representing the old 2nd District since November 2023. A Cedar City native and attorney, she worked as a soil conservationist and then in public lands and water law before serving as counsel to Rep. Chris Stewart, whose seat she won in a 2023 special election. She sits on the Appropriations and Natural Resources committees, chairs the Congressional Western Caucus, and is running on tax cuts, border security and giving Utah more control over federal lands.

background.text: Born in Cedar City, Utah, in 1981 and raised in Hiko, Nevada; graduated from Pahranagat Valley High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in agriculture from Southern Utah University in 2003 and a J.D. from Brigham Young University in 2015.
Began her career as a soil conservationist, which her House website says lasted about a decade working with Utah families and farmers.

After law school, worked as a deputy Washington County attorney, a public lands attorney for the Utah Association of Counties and a staff attorney for the Washington County Water Conservancy District.
Served as chief legal counsel to Rep. Chris Stewart before running for his seat.

Won the Republican convention on June 24, 2023, then the September 5, 2023 special Republican primary (38.8%) over Becky Edwards and Bruce Hough, and the November 21, 2023 special general election (56.8%) to succeed Stewart; took office November 28, 2023.
Re-elected in November 2024 with 58.0% of the vote over Democrat Nathaniel Woodward.
In the 2023-2024 term served on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Small Business.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) serves on the Committee on Appropriations, as vice chair of the Interior, Environment and Related Agencies subcommittee and as a member of the Energy and Water Development and Legislative Branch subcommittees, and on the Committee on Natural Resources (Federal Lands; Water, Wildlife and Fisheries subcommittees).
Chairs the Congressional Western Caucus and, according to her House website, holds co-chair roles on the Bipartisan Build America, Bipartisan Wildfire and other caucuses.

priorities.text: Says legislation she helped pass delivered "the largest tax cut in American history," increasing take-home pay by about $10,000 per year for the average family and cutting taxes for 88% of seniors on Social Security.
Says she has voted to cut federal spending and eliminate wasteful spending, citing $9 billion a year in savings from her work on the Appropriations Committee.
Says she supports giving Utah more control over federal lands and resources, and has voted to expand domestic energy production including oil, gas and refining capacity.

positions.summary: Says she believes all human life is sacred and describes herself as standing up for "pro-life values."
positions.quote: Celeste believes all human life is sacred and will stand up for the unborn and our pro-life values in Congress.

positions.summary: Opposes stricter gun laws, saying she will defend Second Amendment rights against what she calls "gun grabbers" in Washington.
positions.quote: Celeste knows the 2nd Amendment is clear – the right of the people to keep and bear Arms, shall not be infringed.

positions.summary: Says she is committed to securing the border and voted to fully fund a border wall and provide funding and technology to Border Patrol agents.
Opposes raising taxes; touts a tax-cut package she says increased take-home pay and cut taxes for most Social Security recipients.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (Vice Chair, Interior Environment and Related Agencies subcommittee) and the House Committee on Natural Resources in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Kent Udell
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot after the primary was canceled

summary.text: Kent Udell is the Democratic nominee for Utah's 3rd Congressional District. Born in Lehi, he is a University of Utah-trained engineer and professor of mechanical engineering who has served on federal advisory boards.

background.text: Born in Lehi, Utah.
Earned a bachelor's degree and a Ph.D. from the University of Utah, according to his Ballotpedia profile.
Career experience includes working as a professor of mechanical engineering and serving on federal advisory boards.
Advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot after the June 23, 2026 primary was canceled.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website content or Candidate Connection survey found beyond basic biographical facts.

candidates.name: Cassie Easley
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the April 25, 2026 Constitution Party convention

summary.text: Cassie Easley is the Constitution Party nominee for Utah's 3rd Congressional District and has run for Congress in Utah before. She lives in Enoch, is a student at Southern Utah University and a certified firearms instructor, and says she is running on strict adherence to the Constitution, Second Amendment rights and limiting federal spending to enumerated powers.

background.text: Describes herself as the daughter of a Navy veteran who grew up as a "Navy brat" and has lived in rural Utah for 20 years; lives in Enoch, Utah.
Is a student at Southern Utah University, studying political science, economics and agriculture and range studies with a minor in legal studies, according to her Ballotpedia survey.
Describes herself as a certified firearms and concealed-carry instructor and member of Gun Owners of America, the National Rifle Association and the United States Concealed Carry Association.
Describes herself as a Constitution Party leader and National Committee member.
Ran as the Constitution Party candidate in the 2023 special election for Utah's 2nd District (2.3%) and in the 2024 general election for the same seat (5.6%).
Says she volunteers with the Utah Food Bank and Operation Christmas Child.

priorities.text: Says her core campaign messages are "We the People," the Second Amendment, and the Sixteenth Amendment.

Says a representative's only two responsibilities are fidelity to the Constitution and to the will of the people they represent, and that federal spending on anything outside constitutionally enumerated powers should not be funded.
priorities.quote: Anything that falls outside of the Constitutional boundaries should not be funded.

positions.summary: Is a strong proponent of the Second Amendment and a certified firearms instructor, opposing stricter gun laws.
positions.quote: I am a strong proponent of the 2nd Amendment, without it there is no way to protect the rest.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website was found; biography draws on her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

candidates.name: Michael Stoddard
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the April 18, 2026 Libertarian Party convention; previously a Libertarian candidate for this district in 2022

summary.text: Michael Stoddard is the Libertarian Party nominee for Utah's 3rd Congressional District. He previously ran for the same office in 2022, finishing third.

background.text: Advanced from the Libertarian Party convention on April 18, 2026.
Ran as the Libertarian candidate for Utah's 3rd Congressional District in 2022, receiving 2.9% (8,287 votes) in a race won by Rep. John Curtis.
